A_target.statement:
Let $f: R \to S$ be a [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]].
Then:
:$R / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$
as [[Definition:Ring (Abstract Algebra)|rings]].

B_source.statement:
Let $f: G \to H$ be a [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|group homomorphism]].
Then:
:$G / \map \ker f \cong \Img f$

validity_conditions: ker(f) of a ring hom is a two-sided ideal, so the quotient ring R/ker(f) is well-defined (the analogue of ker being normal in the group case).
The well-definedness of the induced map and its bijectivity argument carry over verbatim; only the extra multiplicative structure must additionally be checked to be preserved.
proof_plan:
$\map \ker f$ is an additive subgroup, and for $r \in R$, $k \in \map \ker f$:
:$\map f {r k} = \map f r \cdot 0 = 0$
and similarly $\map f {k r} = 0$.
Hence $\map \ker f$ is a two-sided [[Definition:Ideal of Ring|ideal]], the analogue of a normal subgroup.
Define $\bar f: R / \map \ker f \to \Img f$ by $\map {\bar f} {r + \map \ker f} = \map f r$.
By the proof of the [[First Isomorphism Theorem for Groups]] applied to $\struct {R, +}$, $\bar f$ is a well-defined [[Definition:Bijection|bijective]] additive homomorphism.

In addition:
:$\map {\bar f} {\paren {r + \map \ker f} \paren {s + \map \ker f} } = \map f {r s} = \map f r \map f s$
so $\bar f$ is multiplicative, and is a [[Definition:Ring Isomorphism|ring isomorphism]].
{{qed}}
